analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds a new section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' (head lines 4816-4826). The section says plain decode steps commit a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound, via GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers. It states that results do not depend on the partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. The units I was given are base excerpts at lines 838-1644 of the doc. They cover Nemotron Super, GLM5Next, calibration and the request path. They do not include the new section, and the patch excerpt is complete for it. I checked the new text against the threat model. No source code, configuration, authorization, attestation, encryption, wire-protocol, or prefix-cache logic changes. T-041's SSD cache posture (30-minute TTL, HMAC names, account-scoped salt) is not touched. The command-buffer change is a performance tuning claim with no change to trust boundaries or data exposure. It is plausibly relevant only to availability and GPU memory behavior (T-029, T-010). The doc describes a code-side change (GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers, CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding) that is not in the supplied evidence. I cannot verify the implementation, such as whether the larger commit interval could affect cancellation latency, memory retention of intermediate buffers, or wedge detection. That remains an unverified contract, not a finding. No documentation drift against the threat model was identified. The base excerpts are pre-existing text and unchanged here, so I do not restate their issues. Remaining question for integration: whether the matching Swift source change keeps cancellation and watchdog behavior intact under 100-op commits.
